Transient values for a saved profile

html:
HTTP / REST Skill

For routine Proxmox server and guest operations, enable the optional Proxmox VE skill and use its domain tools. It reuses this Gateway HTTP authentication and transport implementation. Its typed Proxmox Server parameter is distinct from the generic HTTP Connection profiles described below; neither creating a profile nor registering a skill enables Proxmox automatically.

Use http.request for HTTP, REST and API work. It is advertised immediately when the selected Gateway supports HTTP. Use curl/wget only when the user explicitly requests them, or native HTTP reports a genuinely unsupported required feature and the task allows an alternative. Explicit user constraints on capabilities must be respected. TLS, authentication, profile and connection-reference failures are recoverable configuration problems; they do not imply that native HTTP is unsupported. Capability Policy remains the authority for deterministic tool exclusion.

Agent chooses endpoint, method and literal connection configuration
  → existing Permission Policy and ExecutionEngine
  → HTTP capability and literal profile and OAuth session state
  → GatewayClient private envelope
  → selected Gateway: auth provider, session, TLS, target socket
  → bounded literal HTTP receipt

The Gateway retains private LAN, VPN, internal DNS and its own localhost reachability. The Agent backend never logs into the destination API. Inbound POST /http/request and outbound WebSocket dispatch use the same Gateway service and transaction engine.

Gateway runtime readiness and updates

After a source update, ./install.sh updates the main application environment and the local Linux or macOS Gateway environment. install-no-build.sh inherits the same setup; AOR_SKIP_GATEWAY_SETUP=1 explicitly opts out for server-only hosts. The platform installers share scripts/update_gateway_runtime.py and the pyproject.toml dependency contract. Installation verifies pip check and mandatory runtime imports, identifies the updated environment and fails if the checks fail. Restart the local Gateway and smTO after updating; installers do not restart them. Run the supported platform installer separately on each remote Gateway host after updating its checkout. Windows uses src/gateway_windows/install.ps1.

GET /capabilities reports http_runtime.ready. A missing mandatory HTTP dependency removes http_request from both capability lists while other usable Gateway capabilities remain available. Before collecting API credentials, the Agent validates the public recipe and probes the selected Gateway's current capabilities over its existing inbound or outbound route. A stale or legacy advertisement without affirmative readiness cannot authorize secret collection. No API credential is sent in that probe.

http_gateway_dependency_missing and http_gateway_runtime_error identify Gateway runtime defects. Repair them by running the supported installer on that Gateway host and restarting it. Endpoint or password changes do not repair a broken environment. A known pre-dispatch failure reports executed=false and effect_unknown=false; a target HTTP 404 remains an observed response with executed=true and status_code=404. A dispatched write whose response is lost retains effect_unknown=true. Error reasons survive into Results. OAuth waits use ordinary activity input; missing literal credentials return an ordinary authentication failure.

Tools and connection discovery

Tool Effect Purpose
http.request Dynamic Structured API request; core when available
http.connect Read Establish a scoped one-off connection from literal authentication values and TLS configuration
http.inspect_connections Read List, search or get connection configuration
http.manage_connection Write, normal confirmation Create, update or delete literal configuration
http.test_connection Read Authenticate if needed and call a bounded configured test endpoint

Discover the three connection tools with discover_tools(skill_ids=["http"]).

{"query":"Proxmox"}

Call http.inspect_connections with that query, observe the returned canonical profile_key, then use it:

{"method":"GET","profile_key":"Proxmox Lab","url":"/api2/json/cluster/resources","query":{"type":"vm"}}

If multiple connections match, ask the user which one. Neither first-row ordering, last use nor credential presence selects a secret profile. An already observed exact key can be used directly. Generic parameters.inspect/manage remains available. The legacy generic execution-value map excludes HTTP profiles. Scalar shell export uses the narrower Auth-protected predicate, so ordinary non-OAuth HTTP types are not categorically excluded; use native HTTP tools for saved-profile and session checks.

Discovery examines the first 1,000 Parameter Store records, then filters them by HTTP type and public key/description/aliases. It does not search credential values. Its complete flag reflects the filtered count, so an empty result does not prove that no later stored profile exists. Use an already observed canonical key for an exact lookup when appropriate. Inspection returns a portable profile as well as metadata: literal credential fields remain visible when PARAMETERS redaction is off. See the connection adapters.

Parameter Store connections and storage

Parameter Store → New → HTTP Connection is the saved connection management surface. Its HTTP Connection tab supports structured configuration, literal credential editing, disconnect and a test from a selected Gateway; normal Parameter controls own metadata, rename and delete. Basic, Bearer, API Key, Session Login and OAuth2 templates are public prefills. The nickname is the Parameter key. Aliases and description support discovery. The editor accepts authentication metadata, TLS configuration, optional session/proxy settings and a test endpoint. Credential inputs show the stored literal values when PARAMETERS is off.

The structured editor starts from the loaded profile and replaces only sections whose controls changed. Untouched optional fields stay as stored. For an older profile without test_request, the displayed 10-second/4-KiB values are draft defaults; leaving that section untouched preserves its absence and the test adapter's defaults described below. Save pending edits before using Test or Disconnect.

A redacted profile cannot be saved through those structured controls. Use the Parameter editor's Reveal & edit value action to work with the actual raw configuration. The structured form does not expose the auth_ref identity and scope fields: an existing unchanged auth_ref section is preserved, while creating or changing those fields requires the raw profile editor. Merely selecting that authentication type does not supply its required reference.

Saved HTTP connections are typed Parameter Store entries. For ordinary HTTP authentication types, @production_api captures the accepted literal profile, including credentials, in the run snapshot. Protected OAuth/auth_ref profiles capture permitted identity projections instead. PARAMETERS controls ordinary model and UI copies independently; execution uses its authorized raw values. Generic execution-value maps exclude all HTTP profiles, but scalar shell export excludes only Auth-protected records. Use the exact saved key with native HTTP tools for profile/session checks. The parameter architecture explains these separate boundaries.

The /api/agent/http/connections/* routes use the same Parameter Store. The editor saves literal provider fields. Disconnect invalidates sessions; delete removes the record and invalidates sessions. Raw reveal remains an explicit audited endpoint.

The settings routes accept JSON objects up to one MiB for save and test requests. Saving requires a profile; an update replaces its portable configuration rather than preserving omitted credential fields. Alias and description changes are applied only when supplied. The retired POST /api/agent/http/connections/{key}/credentials endpoint returns 410; save literal values in the profile instead. Disconnect keeps those stored values.

An explicit settings test resolves the selected/default Gateway and its current capability snapshot before running the ordinary HTTP test adapter. Defaults are GET /, 15 seconds and a 16-KiB response bound, overridden by the saved test_request. Reachability and application success are separate: a received error status can be reachable with ok=false. These UI actions do not create an Agent confirmation wait; model-invoked profile management remains a write tool subject to normal Permission Policy.

The current read/save validator accepts only version 3 profiles with literal provider fields. Version 1/2 profiles, private credential maps and slot references are unsupported. Recreate an old profile using the HTTP Connection editor. For example:

{
  "profile_type": "http_connection",
  "profile_version": 3,
  "base_url": "https://api.example.com/v1/",
  "default_headers": {"Accept": "application/json"},
  "auth": {"type": "bearer"},
  "tls": {"mode": "system"},
  "session": {"ttl_seconds": 3600, "reauthenticate_reads": true},
  "test_request": {"method": "GET", "url": "/health", "timeout_seconds": 15}
}

This example leaves the bearer token unset. Supply the literal auth.token before authentication can succeed. PARAMETERS controls inspection copies; it never changes the stored profile.

Stored credentials use the Parameter Store's existing sensitive-record semantics. This release does not introduce encryption at rest or a new vault/database; protect the existing local storage accordingly.

Literal authentication

HTTP accepts literal authentication values in chat, tool arguments and saved v3 profiles. Missing values use ordinary ask_user; no credential form, volatile password vault or credential-specific wait state is created. OAuth browser/device authorization uses the ordinary user wait with its protocol-specific controls.

Saved profiles keep literal credentials in their v3 provider fields. The current validator rejects legacy private maps and credential slots; normalization does not migrate them. The Redaction settings control consumer copies; new installations enable every switch, while existing settings and accepted snapshots retain their choices. Missing legacy policies fall back to off. Raw authentication, receipts and recovery data remain unchanged by projection.

Authentication providers

Provider Public configuration Literal values / behavior
none None No authentication
auth_ref auth_ref, optional required_scopes Controller Auth Broker resolves a saved OAuth connection into a private lease before Gateway dispatch; see Shared Auth Broker.
basic, digest Optional username username when no hint; password; Requests implementations
bearer None token → Bearer Authorization
api_key_header header_name, optional prefix/suffix value
api_key_query query_name value, optionally projected at URL/HTTP consumers
api_key_cookie cookie_name value, private cookie jar
secret_headers headers:[{name,value,prefix?,suffix?}] Literal header values
session_login login specification below Form/JSON login, cookies and extracted session values
oauth2 Grant and endpoint/client metadata Client credentials, code + PKCE, device authorization and refresh
ntlm Optional username Install .[http-ntlm] on the Gateway; username/password
negotiate None Install .[http-negotiate]; use the Gateway OS credential context through Windows SSPI or, on other platforms, GSSAPI with its native prerequisites.

Optional enterprise dependencies load lazily. Missing prerequisites return http_auth_provider_unavailable; no downgrade to Basic occurs. The source-controlled provider registry is the extension point for signers. AWS SigV4, OAuth1 and private-key JWT are not implemented; profiles cannot contain signing scripts.

The registry selects providers for both validation and execution. Configuration schemas reject undeclared fields and invalid header/extraction rules; they do not prove that a remote service accepts the supplied values. Providers prepare request components or use the existing AuthFlow for a bounded login. The HTTP client owns resource dispatch, session lifetime and TLS transport. Value overlays replace only advertised credential leaves on a copy and revalidate it; they do not persist a corrected password or change the selected provider, origin or TLS policy.

Generic session login and Proxmox examples

An API-token connection needs no service-specific client:

{
  "profile_type":"http_connection",
  "profile_version":3,
  "base_url":"https://pve.example.internal:8006",
  "auth":{"type":"api_key_header","header_name":"Authorization","prefix":"PVEAPIToken="}
}

Set auth.value to the complete token credential.

A generic password/session profile expresses the ticket and CSRF flow entirely in metadata:

{
  "profile_type":"http_connection",
  "profile_version":3,
  "base_url":"https://pve.example.internal:8006",
  "auth":{
    "type":"session_login",
    "login":{
      "path":"/api2/json/access/ticket",
      "method":"POST",
      "body_mode":"form",
      "fields":{
        "username":"root@pam",
        "password":"example-password"
      },
      "success_codes":[200],
      "extract":[
        {"source":"json","path":"/data/ticket","target":"cookie","name":"PVEAuthCookie"},
        {"source":"json","path":"/data/CSRFPreventionToken","target":"header","name":"CSRFPreventionToken","methods":["POST","PUT","PATCH","DELETE"]}
      ]
    }
  },
  "tls":{"mode":"custom_ca","ca_certificate":"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"},
  "test_request":{"method":"GET","url":"/api2/json/cluster/resources"}
}

body_mode can be form or json. Fields are literal scalars, including username and password. Login is a bounded internal POST, not a second resource-mutation approval. Login redirects never carry credentials elsewhere.

Extraction supports RFC 6901 JSON pointers, named response headers and the actual cookie jar. Apply values to a cookie, header, query parameter or JSON/form body. methods restricts injection, and body injection requires explicitly configured mutating methods. Cookie and CSRF values remain available to the protocol and raw receipts; optional HTTP projection controls previews.

An expected login success status alone is insufficient when an API returns a ticket in JSON without setting a reusable cookie. Missing or incomplete extraction produces http_session_mapping_required, classified as authentication_configuration. It means credentials were not rejected; inspect authoritative API documentation and correct session_cookie, session_values and/or CSRF extraction. Login bodies and returned tickets are never exposed in that error. The literal recipe remains available for the next attempt.

Connection recipes retain literal authentication. Correcting extraction/session/test settings can establish a fresh session using those values. Saved revisions and run-scoped connection references retain their existing validation.

The Agent interprets /cluster/resources data and identifies running guests. Production HTTP code contains no VM filtering, PVE URL construction or service-specific parser.

OAuth 2

Use auth.type=oauth2 and grant_type=client_credentials, authorization_code or device_authorization. Configure client_id, token_endpoint, optional scope, audience/resource, and client_auth=client_secret_basic|client_secret_post|none|tls_client_auth.

For authorization code, configure authorization_endpoint and the exact redirect_uri:

https://your-smto-host/api/agent/http/oauth/callback

The OAuth UI opens authorization. State, PKCE S256 verifier, expiry and single-use exchange are runtime-owned; callbacks cannot forward arbitrary redirects. The callback log filter removes query strings for the recognized controller OAuth callback routes before ordinary optional log redaction, preserving the access logger's formatting contract. For device authorization, configure device_authorization_endpoint; the OAuth UI shows the verification page and user code. The runtime polls with provider intervals, authorization_pending, slow_down, denial and expiry handling.

Known access-token expiry triggers refresh before the resource call. Supplied access/refresh tokens can initialize a session. Newly exchanged session tokens remain in the HTTP session cache; callers may explicitly save literal token fields in a profile.

An issuer enables OIDC metadata discovery with exact issuer validation. Discovered endpoints must remain on a configured approved origin. If a provider uses a separate auth origin, add it explicitly to allowed_origins. OAuth resource-owner password grant is deliberately rejected.

TLS, mTLS and proxies

TLS belongs to http.connect or a saved profile. Passing tls or other connection-only fields to http.request is strictly rejected with http_connect_required: call http.connect with the connection settings, then use its exact returned connection_ref. The request schema does not accept TLS.

TLS modes are system (default), custom_ca or explicitly configured insecure. The UI prominently displays TLS certificate verification disabled for insecure profiles. A certificate failure returns http_tls_verification_failed with failure_class=tls and recoverable_with_http=true. Prefer a trusted private CA using custom_ca. Explicit insecure keeps HTTPS encryption but disables certificate identity verification for that connection. A certificate failure never causes an automatic insecure retry or a curl fallback. allow_insecure_http is a legacy compatibility field; literal credentials are accepted on HTTP without this switch.

Custom CA accepts a Gateway-local ca_path or ca_certificate. mTLS accepts paired client_cert_path/client_key_path, or paired client_certificate/client_key. Paths refer to the selected Gateway, never the Agent server. Literal PEM material uses unique temporary files with restricted permissions and cleanup. The same options apply to resource requests and OAuth client authentication.

Explicit proxy.http/proxy.https URLs are supported, with optional literal username and password. trust_env=False prevents inherited proxy credentials and netrc behavior.

Literal credentials are permitted over HTTP and HTTPS. Explicit TLS configuration and Gateway identity verification still apply; redaction does not change either.

Requests, files and results

GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are reads. Other valid HTTP method tokens are writes; CONNECT and TRACE are blocked. Standard write confirmation remains unchanged. Ordinary auth handshakes execute internally after the operation has been authorized.

Use one body mode: native json_body, UTF-8 text_body, form_body, multipart_body or body_reference. Read methods cannot carry a body. Inline JSON/text/form bodies are bounded to 1 MiB. Serialized JSON objects/arrays still return json_body_appears_serialized; supply native JSON instead.

{
  "method":"POST",
  "url":"https://api.example.com/upload",
  "multipart_body":{
    "fields":{"description":"Report"},
    "files":[{"name":"file","context_id":"ctx_observed_reference"}]
  }
}

Use an actual observed/granted context ID. No arbitrary file paths or inline base64 file copies are accepted. body_reference:{context_id:...} sends a granted source as raw bytes. Aggregate referenced content is bounded to 8 MiB to fit both Gateway transports.

The file adapter counts each referenced part against that aggregate budget, including repeated IDs. In the current error handler an oversized upload is reported as http_context_unavailable; check both source grants and total size when investigating that result. This rejection occurs before the HTTP request is dispatched.

Inline responses default to 256 KiB and are capped at 2 MiB. response_mode=artifact allows a bounded response up to 8 MiB; set max_response_bytes explicitly for larger downloads. The Gateway reads a bounded raw stream and returns a transfer envelope; the Agent retains it as a granted ContextStore source. The model receives a context ID, byte count, media type and SHA-256, not megabytes of base64. Temporary buffering is bounded; downloads are not unlimited.

Response retention happens after transport completes. An artifact decoding or storage failure does not prove that the remote operation was never executed. The request adapter raises an unknown-outcome signal for lost or invalid write receipts, preserving the need for reconciliation before retrying a mutation. Saved-profile usage is recorded before upload/retention validation, so a use counter is not a count of successful requests.

Results retain method, URL, status/reason, headers, content type, body/encoding, bytes read, truncation/completeness, redirects, Gateway and execution status. Raw headers may include Set-Cookie. Optional HTTP projection masks the consumer copy without changing status, raw bytes or artifacts.

Gateway transaction ownership

The request contract performs pure method, URL, origin, header and body validation. It produces a prepared request for the transaction owner, which acquires a session, installs TLS options and invokes the selected provider. Authentication and resource requests share the request's monotonic deadline.

flowchart LR Input[Arguments and selected profile] --> Validate[Validate and encode] Validate --> Session[Acquire scoped session] Session --> Auth[Prepare authentication] Auth --> Resource[Dispatch resource request] Resource --> Read[Bound and decode response] Read --> Result[Receipt and activity projection] Resource --> Expired{Definitive 401 on a read?} Expired -->|Eligible once| Auth

The session cache retains at most 128 identities by default. A cache identity includes the complete profile, target origin and private runtime scope, excluding transient OAuth runtime fields. Calls without a scope, and calls beyond cache capacity, use disposable sessions. A session lock serializes authentication and requests for the same identity; waiting checks cancellation. Clearing expired authentication removes cookies and derived values while retaining prior secret provenance until disposal, so late echoed credentials can still be recognized.

Bound Current implementation
Request timeout 30 seconds by default; accepted range 1–120 seconds
URL At most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes
Request headers At most 64 headers and 32 KiB including separators
Redirects Disabled by default; at most five when enabled
Authentication response 64 KiB decoded-response budget
Resource response 256 KiB default; up to 2 MiB inline or 8 MiB as an artifact
Compressed response input Decoded budget plus 64 KiB encoded-input allowance

The reader supports identity, gzip and deflate encodings. It reports unsupported encodings, incomplete input and truncation separately from HTTP status. A complete JSON response becomes a native value; invalid/incomplete JSON remains text, and binary media uses a private transfer/base64 envelope until the controller projects or retains it. Encoding helpers do not themselves redact values.

Cancellation ownership associates an execution ID with its sockets. Cancellation closes active I/O and remembers the ID for five minutes to stop a delayed dispatch. It cannot undo a remote write. Activity capture is a separate presentation boundary: private context fields and binary bodies are structurally removed, then the selected ACTIVITY policy applies credential masking. Private OAuth flows require protection regardless of optional switches. An observation failure must not change request or retry behavior.

Relevant isolated scenarios cover wire values, upload/download envelopes, authentication evidence and socket cancellation.

Sessions, origins and failures

Gateway sessions are memory-only, bounded and synchronized. Identity includes run/connection, profile revision, credential material, Gateway instance and resource origin. Profile changes, credential replacement, delete, disconnect and run termination revoke reachable sessions through the private Gateway control envelope. If a Gateway is disconnected, old state is unreachable through the new identity. Unused cached sessions older than one hour are removed on a later acquisition; this is opportunistic cleanup, not a background expiry timer. No cookies are persisted to disk.

Explicit authenticated URLs must remain on the profile origin or a configured allowed origin. //attacker.example cannot escape this check. Authenticated redirects remain on the current approved request origin; cross-origin forwarding and scheme downgrade are blocked by default.

A read with a definitive expired session can reauthenticate and retry once if session.reauthenticate_reads permits. A write is never automatically replayed on session expiry or ambiguous transport failure. Lost mutation responses still produce HttpMutationOutcomeUnknown. A failed login can report an executed authentication endpoint with resource_executed=false; it does not imply an executed resource mutation.

Errors distinguish missing/rejected credentials, unavailable providers, expired sessions, OAuth authorization/denial/expiry/state, TLS failure, invalid/missing profiles, unsafe target/Gateway transport and unavailable file contexts. ERRORS optionally projects diagnostic copies.

One-off connections and recovery

For a new endpoint, call http.connect with base_url, literal auth values and optional tls. A literal recipe is retained during OAuth authorization, but only a successful connection is advertised in CURRENT TASK. Use the exact returned connection_ref with http.request; never invent or edit it. An unavailable reference requires an exact established reference or a new http.connect call. References remain scoped to the run, origin and selected Gateway. Saved profiles remain in Parameter Store.

For generic session login, configure login_path, body_mode, literal username and password, field names and documented extraction paths. Successful login still requires valid session extraction or a returned cookie. JSON extraction uses JSON Pointer.

Literal credentials are accepted in Shell, Web and ordinary HTTP fields. HTTP response receipts retain execution truth: a received 404 remains an executed response. Recovery never automatically replays mutations.

Verified setup across Conversation turns

Working Context can retain successful HTTP setup separately from response evidence. A saved connection projects its exact profile key, Gateway identity, base URL, authentication kind and TLS configuration. A reproducible one-off setup projects literal http.connect arguments. It does not carry a live connection reference into a new run, or make an earlier node status, response body or permission decision current.

The HTTP setup adapter validates canonical configuration and decides which failures make setup stale. Configuration, authentication and transport errors can stale a matching setup; an ordinary HTTP application status such as 404 does not do so by itself. A changed saved profile must be reverified. One-off recipes that cannot be faithfully reconstructed are omitted from this optional continuity mechanism without changing the successful HTTP receipt.

The connection registry holds at most 32 recipes per run. Capturing a recipe is provisional, including when an identical existing recipe is recaptured; only successful establishment makes it an executable choice. Resolution checks the run, current Gateway and bound origin. The per-decision tool projection copies the catalog and lists only established current references. A historical, provisional or foreign reference cannot become authority merely because it appears in earlier messages.

When the HTTP reuse Agent Check is enabled, the reuse guard can focus the next decision on one unambiguous verified setup:

flowchart TD Request[Proposed HTTP request] --> Check{Current reference or explicit saved key?} Check -->|Yes| Validate[Ordinary HTTP and permission validation] Check -->|No| Match{One compatible verified setup?} Match -->|Saved profile| Profile[Require exact profile key] Match -->|One-off with current reference| Reference[Require matching current reference] Match -->|One-off without current reference| Connect[Require verified connect recipe] Profile --> Decision[Next model decision] Reference --> Decision Connect --> Decision Match -->|Ambiguous| NoChoice[Do not select a resource]

The guard constrains connection authority; the model still chooses the resource method, path and body. It never picks the most recently used setup to resolve ambiguity. An invented reference is rejected even when no single setup can be selected. Explicit alternate configuration returns to normal validation; malformed authentication or TLS values cannot escape an existing focus. Capability exclusions and write approvals still apply. Temporal routing takes precedence, and required-tool provider options are added only when the final projection is exactly the focused tool and the client supports that keyword.

Two correction opportunities are allowed; a third rejected attempt blocks the run. Rejected calls report executed=false and do not stale the verified setup. Their no-dispatch fact is saved before the ordinary receipt boundary, so recovery can restore that rejection without treating it as an unknown remote effect. User steering releases focus; normal completion/failure releases it after the relevant call, while credential, approval and budget waits retain it.

OAuth wait and resume ownership

The HTTP session owner keeps callback state and authorization codes in process memory. Callbacks require an unconsumed state, matching redirect URI and unexpired interaction. Device polling uses the existing wait worker. The checkpoint retains the exact undispatched tool continuation and its authorization decision; resuming journals a new claimed call before dispatch and reuses the normal receipt boundary. This avoids an additional model decision without bypassing operation ownership.

After process restart, an absent volatile interaction is exposed as an expired authorization requiring an ordinary reply. It is not restored from an old browser code. Run retirement deactivates its recipe registry and clears run-owned auth; conversation-owned auth has a separate lifetime. Gateway invalidation is best effort after local cleanup. Opportunistic idle-entry cleanup is not a background timer or proof that a disconnected Gateway received an invalidation.

The reuse scenarios and cross-turn scenarios cover these boundaries with scripted inference and fake or local HTTP services. Some full-turn callbacks retain older inline-receipt expectations; their results are recorded in the repository's documentation review ledger, separately from direct guard and registry checks.

Transient values for a saved profile

http.connect({"profile_key":"Lab API","auth_values":{"username":"user", "password":"literal value"}}) applies the values to a copy for the returned connection. It never edits Parameter Store. Missing/rejected results advertise missing_fields/retry_fields for a normal Agent question and retry. Supported paths are provider leaves such as token, value, client_secret, login.fields.<name>, headers.<name>.value, and proxy username/password. These paths cannot change provider type, URLs, header names, extraction, TLS or origins.

The profile digest is bound when the connection is established. Editing its saved configuration invalidates that reference; reconnect using the new configuration. Saving credentials remains an explicit profile-management operation.

Shared Auth Broker

A saved v3 HTTP connection may use auth: {"type":"auth_ref", "auth_ref":"work_identity","required_scopes":["api.read"]} to consume a generic Parameter Store OAuth connection. The controller's Auth Broker obtains and refreshes tokens; a revision-bound private lease supplies the selected verified Gateway immediately before a resource request. An unresolved auth_ref reaching the Gateway fails closed. Existing inline HTTP OAuth profiles retain their supported v3 interface through auth/http_compat.py. New shared connections use the generic /api/agent/auth/oauth/callback; existing callback routes remain compatible. See Auth and Email.
